name: ISO/IEC 42001
what: Certifiable management system standard for AI: policies, roles, risk and impact assessment across the AI lifecycle
status: No amendments. Companion standards cover impact assessment (ISO/IEC 42005, May 2025) and certification bodies (ISO/IEC 42006, July 2025). UKAS accredited BSI as the first UK certification body in January 2026

name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
what: Voluntary framework to govern, map, measure and manage AI risks, with profiles for specific uses
version: AI RMF 1.0, plus the Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1, July 2024)
status: Being revised under the US AI Action Plan; no revised version yet. Concept note for a critical infrastructure profile published April 2026

group: Threat modelling and secure AI development
name: MITRE ATLAS
what: Knowledge base of adversary tactics and techniques against AI systems, modelled on ATT&CK, with real-world case studies
version: Living knowledge base, released monthly (latest v2026.11)
status: November 2026 release (v2026.11) adds ARTEX case studies, hardware attack techniques and new threat actor entries, and renames 'AI Agent Tools' to 'Agentic AI'. Now 16 tactics, 137 techniques, 98 sub-techniques, 44 mitigations and 85 case studies. Monthly releases continued from June to November 2026

group: Threat modelling and secure AI development
name: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications
what: The ten most critical security risks for applications built on large language models
status: Released with a new Agent Control Standard. Sits alongside the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications

group: Threat modelling and secure AI development
name: Guidelines for secure AI system development
owner: NCSC and CISA, with international partners
what: Guidance on secure design, development, deployment, and operation and maintenance of AI systems
status: No update since 2023. Built on by the DSIT AI Cyber Security Code of Practice and ETSI EN 304 223

group: Threat modelling and secure AI development
name: AI Cyber Security Code of Practice
what: Voluntary UK baseline of security principles for developers and operators of AI systems, with an implementation guide
status: Basis for the European standard ETSI EN 304 223 (December 2025). The Code is due to be updated to align with it

name: ISO/IEC 27001
what: Certifiable information security management system standard, with Annex A controls
status: No AI-specific requirements. Often used alongside ISO/IEC 42001

name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework
what: Outcomes to govern, identify, protect, detect, respond and recover, used to set and assess cyber security targets
status: Cyber AI Profile (NIST IR 8596) in preliminary draft since December 2025; comments closed January 2026, next draft awaited

name: Cyber Assessment Framework (CAF)
what: Outcome-based framework for assessing the cyber resilience of essential services, used by UK regulators and the NHS
status: Version 4.0 added outcomes on AI-related risks. Further versions expected to follow the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill

name: Data Security and Protection Toolkit (DSPT)
what: Annual self-assessment for organisations with access to NHS patient data and systems; CAF-aligned for larger NHS organisations
status: 2026-27 standard published with updated CAF-aligned audit guidance
